acceptance: The five files on site main match their content before #209.
The deployed pages no longer state a 3000 maximum or a shortened official list.
context: Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).
description:
## Problem
benchbox-site #209 (1f5a50f7e8) merged to `main` and deployed to benchbox.dev. Nine sentences on five pages say tpcds and tpcds_obt stop at scale factor 3000 and that TPC-DS official scale factors are 1 to 3000. Released v0.5.1 accepts up to 100000 including 10000, 30000 and 100000. The site's AGENTS.md sends documentation of unreleased behaviour to `next`, and the owner decided on 2026-11-17 to leave `main` alone until the next release pin.

## Change
One pull request to benchbox-site `main` restoring the pre-#209 text in docs/benchmarks/index.md, docs/concepts/benchmark-methodology.md, docs/contributing-results.md, docs/reference/python-api/benchmarks/tpcds.md and tpcds-obt.md. The #209 text also reached `next` through the main-to-next sync (#213, fb41371); removing it there is site-next-remove-tpcds-3000-limit-text-20261120, after the core restore merges. In the sync that follows this revert, keep next's dsdgen floor reason.

## Decision gates
None: this restores text that matches the released version. Do not add new wording about query 9 or the dsdgen floor reason, which is unreleased.

## Verification rubric
Pass: `git diff 1f5a50f7e8^ <new main>` is empty for the five files; `npm run lint:docs` and `npm run docs:check` pass; after deploy, the five live pages contain no '3000' limit statement (fetch and grep).

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label id or text is shown to the owner before it is committed. Briefs quote owner answers verbatim; questions to the owner carry no preselected answer.
- The implementer replies on review threads and leaves resolving them to the reviewer or the owner, unless the owner says otherwise (AGENTS.md asks agents to resolve benchbox-oracle threads on soundness paths; the owner has been asked which applies).
- Hosted writes (merge, close, disable or enable auto-merge, workflow dispatch, remote branch delete) only as the repository's close-out procedure or the owner's word for that pull request allows; never raw `gh pr merge` in core.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted. Push only after `make pr-preflight` exits 0 on the exact head.
- No worktree takeover while another session may be working; no tracker write from a server that reports a stale version; never chain `git stash` with `git stash pop`.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point, one run at a time.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
